title: Chapter 1 Revision — Aspect Pairs Fundamentals
description: Mixed revision quiz covering perfective/imperfective concept, common aspect pairs, semantic groups, and aspect in paragraph context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence implies the speaker DID finish reading the book?
questions.explanation: 'Przeczytałem' = perfective past — I read through (and finished) this book. 'Czytałem' = imperfective past — I was reading this book (may not have finished). Perfective guarantees completion.

questions.prompt: Which aspect is expected after negation in 'Nie ___ tej książki' (I haven't read this book)?
questions.explanation: After negation, imperfective is standard: 'Nie czytałem tej książki' = I haven't read this book (general negation of the activity). 'Nie przeczytałem' is also possible but means specifically 'I didn't finish reading it'.

questions.prompt: What is the perfective of 'brać' (to take)?
questions.explanation: 'Wziąć' = perfective of brać (suppletive pair — different root). 'Wezmę' = I will take. 'Wziąłem/wzięłam' = I took. Must memorise as irregular. 'Zabrać' = to take away (different meaning).

questions.prompt: Jutro ___ email do klientów. (Tomorrow she will send an email to clients.) [perf future]
questions.explanation: 'Wyśle' = perfective future of wysłać (she will send = completed dispatch). 'Jutro' + single completed action = perfective. 'Będzie wysyłać' = imperfective future (will be in process of sending).
'Przepraszać' (imperf) / 'przeprosić' (perf) = to apologise. 'Przepraszam' = I'm sorry/excuse me (ongoing). 'Przeprosiłem' = I apologised (completed act). The other pairs mean: ask, thank, say.

questions.prompt: W końcu ___ ten artykuł. (She finally understood this article.) [perception, result achieved]
questions.explanation: 'Zrozumiała' = perfective past — she understood/grasped it (moment of comprehension, result). 'W końcu' + perfective. 'Rozumiała' = was understanding (ongoing process without guarantee of completion).

questions.prompt: In this narrative, which aspect is correct for the background action? 'Kiedy ___ w ogrodzie, zaczął padać deszcz.'
questions.explanation: Background ongoing action in kiedy clause → imperfective. Any of 'pracowałam/pracowałem/pracowała' depending on gender of subject. 'Zaczął padać deszcz' = perfective event that interrupted. Option 0 is the correct form for a female speaker.

questions.prompt: Recipe: ___ jajka z cukrem. (Beat eggs with sugar.) [recipe imperative]
questions.explanation: Recipe steps → perfective imperative: 'Ubij' = beat (complete the action). 'Ubijaj' = imperfective imperative (keep beating — ongoing) which could be used for 'continue stirring' type instructions, but not as initial instruction. 'Ubij' = do this action completely.

'Szukać' (imperf) = to look for / search (process). 'Znaleźć' (perf) = to find (result achieved). 'Szukam pracy' = I'm looking for work (ongoing). 'Znalazłam pracę!' = I found a job! (result). The pair: process + result.

questions.prompt: Muszę ___ raport przed piątkiem. (I must complete the report by Friday.) [modal + perf inf]
questions.explanation: 'Muszę napisać' = I must write (= complete) the report. Perfective infinitive after modal when result/completion is intended. 'Muszę pisać' = I need to be in the process of writing (less natural with a deadline).

questions.prompt: Aspect pair for 'to promise': which is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Obiecywać' (imperf) / 'obiecać' (perf) = to promise. 'Zawsze obiecuje ale nie dotrzymuje słowa' (always promises, habit — imperf). 'Obiecałem wrócić' = I promised to come back (specific promise — perf).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sequence: 'Najpierw ___ kawę, a potem ___ pracę.' (First she made coffee, then she started work.)
questions.explanation: Sequential narrative with 'najpierw...a potem' → both perfective: 'zrobiła' (made = completed) + 'zaczęła' (started = began). Sequential completed events use perfective in Polish.
